## Before class

- Read: Stanton **Ch. 2** (Reasoning with Probability)
- Read: R4DS **[Ch. 3 — Data transformation](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html)** and **[Ch. 4 — Workflow: code style](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-style.html)**
- Bring your laptop with R, RStudio, and the course packages installed ([install guide](../resources.qmd#installing-r-and-rstudio))

## In class

- Homework 2 debrief — questions on descriptives
- What a probability *is*: long-run proportion, seen by simulation (coin flips, then real arrest data)
- Toast drops: outcome tables, the binomial distribution, `rbinom()`, cumulative probabilities
- Contingency tables: marginal, joint, and conditional probability — dropped toast, the restaurant work schedule, and arrest × crime category in the Chicago data
- Conditional probability as *filter, then re-proportion* — the seed of Bayes' theorem
- Independence: when conditioning doesn't move the number
- In-class exercise: factory-accidents contingency table (paper, then dplyr — folded into Lab 3)
- **Lab 3:** data transformation with dplyr (`filter`, `arrange`, `mutate`, `summarize`, `count`) using the `neighborhoods` data
